hook:
A FIGHTER PEAKED 
EARLY THIS WEEK 
ON THE WHITEBOARD

caption:
Coaches incorrectly assume that adding volume throughout a fight camp is the key to success. This approach often leads to peaking too early and having nothing left for the actual fight.

The science is clear: peak physical conditioning occurs when volume is tapered in the last ten days of camp. 
During this phase athletes experience a significant increase in power output and speed.

Instead of pushing athletes too hard coaches should focus on identifying peak week and adjusting volume accordingly. 
A coach who understands load management will quietly observe that his athletes are always strongest on fight night.

Every decision made before the warm-up starts. No gut feeling. No guessing. No apologies on Saturday.

The coaches who protect careers are the ones who had the number before anyone walked through the door.
